method: Official XRI devices with queued Input System XR state events

checks.detail: Runtime, world-space UI and original skin structure must initialize.
The test runs without --learning-qa and must depend on actual XR tracking.
LearningSimulatorSetup must install the official XRI XRDeviceSimulator with simulator, controller and required hand sample action assets.
The installed simulator must create an HMD plus both handed controllers; this harness never calls AddDevice.
The official keyboard/mouse sample actions are enabled and the lifecycle manager is configured for controller interaction before deterministic fixture injection.
Disabling only the simulator input writer must retain its virtual devices.
Camera and LabHandInteractor transforms follow queued simulator local poses through LearningXRInput; focused=True
Both official tracked controller devices have one visible left/right glove representation.
The rendered glove is a weighted mesh with five distinct proximal finger bones (thumb, index, middle, ring, little).
The hand appearance has no colliders or rigidbodies that could intercept selection, cutting or instrument contact.
Visible tracked hand geometry belongs only to the glove; no controller model or inactive dissection tool is rendered at sign-in.
The rendered glove is a weighted mesh with five distinct proximal finger bones (thumb, index, middle, ring, little).
The hand appearance has no colliders or rigidbodies that could intercept selection, cutting or instrument contact.
Visible tracked hand geometry belongs only to the glove; no controller model or inactive dissection tool is rendered at sign-in.
Each glove follows the position and rotation of its own tracked controller root without altering the interaction origin.
Moving the visible hands does not replace, offset, or detach the learner's HMD camera.
An actual right trigger event bends the rendered index while the middle finger and opposite hand stay at rest.
A partial grip produces an intermediate visible finger curl from the same analog input used by the official simulator.
Full right grip curls middle, ring and little fingers further than partial grip while leaving the left hand independent.
Releasing the real analog controls returns the rendered fingers to their relaxed pose without a stale clenched hand.
The left trigger and grip animate the left glove without driving the right glove.
When only the left device loses tracking, its glove disappears instead of freezing in space; the right glove stays visible.
Loss of HMD tracking hides both glove renderers and retains the existing interaction pause.
A still-tracked controller aimed at the actual guest button cannot send pointer-down or click events while HMD tracking and hand visibility are lost.
Actual grip and controller movement across the console header cannot drag the panel while the learner's HMD tracking is unavailable.
Tracking recovery restores both visuals without replaying a held trigger as a new Menu press or later click; appearance checks have not activated UI or gameplay.
Initial screen=Sign in
Actual adapter trigger=True
Queued trigger down/up must activate the actual world-space guest button. Screen=Career
The actual orientation UI button opens its first guarded step.
Original skin must be an active mesh collider and XRI grab interactable.
The actual outer skin must be exposed from the simulated learner's view.
First physics hit=A_FMA7163
A real trigger selects the skin, advances only to the grip instruction, and does not complete orientation.
Holding the actual controller Menu button opens one pause menu without interrupting orientation or clearing its current step.
A real grip and hand movement while the menu is open cannot acquire or move anatomy or grant orientation credit.
The next controller Menu press returns to the same workspace, selected skin and orientation step without restarting or completing it.
With HMD tracking false, grip cannot acquire or move anatomy and cannot complete orientation.
Restoring the real tracked device state restores the normal interaction gate; focused=True
A released controller must not reacquire anatomy from a stale grip when HMD tracking returns. Acquires=0 releases=0
XRI selectEntered count=1; interactor selected=1
Stationary grip must not snap the skin pivot to the controller. Displacement=0.0000 m.
A real grab/release with no deliberate hand displacement leaves orientation on its lift step.
The learner can regrip after a stationary release; XRI acquires=2
Commanded hand lift=0.1200 m; measured skin displacement=0.1200 m. Lifting alone must not complete orientation.
Only the actual XRI selectExited release completes orientation. Releases=2
The real skin returns to its anatomical rest pose after the introductory lift.
Captured interface is the actual world-space Unity canvas.
The ordinary StartActivity entry point opens unlocked Easy pneumothorax practice with actual tracked simulator devices.
The real case begins at its anatomical finding; no objective completion has been injected.
Initial case target MAL_RUL has a physically exposed surface.
First actual case ray hit=A_MAL_RUL
The real trigger records the finding and reveals the current assessment pointer on its tray.
The unchanged grab collider is physically reachable and dynamic attachment preserves the held instrument pose.
First instrument ray hit=Assessment pointer
The actual queued controller grip causes one XRI selectEntered on the current procedure instrument.
Stationary instrument pickup: body displacement=0.0000 m, working-end displacement=0.0000 m, rotation=0.00 degrees.
Commanded translation=(0.04, 0.07, -0.03); body error=0.0000 m and working-end error=0.0000 m.
A 22 degree hand turn preserves the dynamic grip offset: body error=0.0000 m, working-end error=0.0000 m, angle error=0.00 degrees.
Real grip release causes one XRI selectExited. The kinematic instrument stays at the released pose when the controller moves away.
Pickup, translation, rotation and release without treatment activation cannot grant procedure credit or append clinical actions.
